P1.evidence: Full four-part frame delivered verbatim: 'where you are today in terms of fitness, where you want to go, what's getting in the way and what you genuinely need to get there', followed by frame agreement ('That sound good.' - 'Yeah, for sure') and the open question 'what could we potentially help you with man?'. Setter notes were only gestured at ('I went over a couple things briefly with you, so I have a bit of a head start'), not read back.

P2.evidence: Complete baseline sweep. Age 29, 6'1", 74-78 kg; 'you said work, obviously UX designer, you said you try and stand a lot, like what percentage is standing'; 'Any health conditions at all?'; 'when did that start? how long has that been?'; yoga and gym frequency; 'what's been your results like with the gym currently?'; 'Itai, walk me through your diet'; 'How's sleep?' plus hours and quality; 'How's energy throughout the day?'

P3.evidence: Strong on surface goals - 'If you could change one thing about your body, like what would be the number one thing to change' - and did drive to legacy via the parents and the niece and nephew ('simple things like picking them up, bending down'). But the parents came from the prospect first; the rep followed rather than led. No explicit 'outside of the physical, what's actually driving this' bridge, and no reflect-back. Instead of reflecting the deep why the rep asserted it: 'I get the sense you just don't have a clear vision for where you'd like things to be' - the prospect only conceded 'Yeah, that could be true'.

P4.evidence: 'What have we tried to actually fix that up to this point' and 'did any of it help at all' both run; physio, chiro and a past personal trainer surfaced. 'What has you be committed or not committed?' and 'what do you think the roadblocks have been?' asked. But when the prospect could not name the gap ('I don't know. It's a good question'), the rep named it for him rather than letting him land it, and never ran the 'the information isn't the problem - why can't you stick to it on your own?' move.

P5.evidence: Consequence question asked well: 'if we don't figure out a system or a way to address some of these aches and pains, like, where do you think you'll be in five years? 10 years?'. The prospect deflected - 'I don't really want to think about that' - and the rep let it go instead of pressing 'is that something you're willing to settle for?' and 'why not?'. Did land the line in the sand: 'do you feel like it is time to draw a line in the sand, or how do you feel?'

P6.evidence: Both belief and commitment questions asked - 'do you feel like that can get you what we talked about in terms of goals?' and 'are you in a point where you are really fully committed to showing up, doing the work'. But the answer to the belief question was a hedge - 'Ideally. I mean, hopefully' - and the rep presented price anyway rather than returning to Phase 5. The unresolved doubt resurfaced at 00:57:23 and cost the call.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and a payment plan offered, but the prospect declined to commit on the call - 'I'm not committing to it right now' - so payment, the Trevor onboarding call, the agreement and the welcome-email steps were never reachable.

objection_plays.detail: Isolate ran cleanly ('finances aside' framing and the logistics-versus-uncertainty split: 'is it more a matter of like, hey, dude, logistically, like it is a little bit tight right now... Or is it more a fact of like, hey, dude, I have the money'). The HOW-not-SHOULD reframe ran ('we're not in a place where it's like, should I do this... It's more a matter of like, how'). Permission for the money conversation was asked for and granted - 'are you open to having just an honest conversation about where we're actually financially'. Then the whole financial picture was skipped: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus after bills, no credit-card count, no available credit, no investments. The rep went straight from permission to inventing a six-payment structure, which is exactly the step the script puts last.

Trigger clear at 00:55:44 ('I would like to have a think about it'). The rep did run the belief question and the 1-10 value rating, but none of the core OA moves landed: no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here', no 'that man you want to be - how does HE decide right now'. The rep abandoned OA and switched to the fear play instead.

Fear and jadedness surfaced ('there's probably some jadedness that's just not going to go right', 'I'm also cautious with... a sort of like silver bullet sort of approach'). The rep normalised it, ran BURNED BEFORE almost to script (asked about the ended relationship then 'just because one relationship didn't work out well, does that mean we never get in another relationship again?'), ran the attractive-versus-unattractive stranger frame to establish that fear scales with stakes, and closed with the PLANE analogy. Only miss inside the play was the explicit 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty'.

Value against a cheaper substitute - 'I'm also wondering if there's other, other methodologies that I could be following that would not cost me six grand'. This is the documented script gap. The rep improvised a differentiation claim ('there is nobody else that does what Trevor does. Like, it's just facts') plus a teach-a-man-to-fish reframe. It worked well enough that the prospect conceded value, but nothing in the playbook supports it and the rep had to invent it live.

Pricing-transparency complaint at 01:05:00 - 'the fact that there was no indication anywhere of prices beforehand, it is a little bit frustrating as a consumer'. There is no scripted response to a prospect objecting to the sales process itself. The rep did not acknowledge it and pivoted straight back to asking whether the payment plan was possible.

notes: Baseline and framing were textbook; the call was lost between P3 and P6. The rep supplied the prospect's 'why' instead of extracting it, let the consequence question be deflected, and pushed past a clear hedge ('hopefully') into the price reveal, so the doubt was still live when the money conversation started. Coaching priority: hold P5b/P5c when a prospect says 'I don't really want to think about that', and do not move off P6 on a maybe. Second priority: run the full OC financial picture before improvising any payment structure.
